remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
I'm feeling spicy tonight so let me just say it:

I think Opus 4.6 was the Opus model with the best personality and writing style.

Something's off with Opus 5 - it tends to give me overly long replies, use Claude-speak way too much (e.g., "here's the honest truth"), and is too judgemental. 

Opus used to be a joy to talk to like a trusted friend. Not so much anymore.
remarks.translation: 今晚我有点火气，就直接说了：我觉得Opus 4.6是Opus系列里个性和文风最棒的模型。Opus 5有点不对劲——它回复总是太长，动不动就用“Claude腔”（比如“说实话”），还爱指手画脚。以前的Opus聊起来像知心朋友，让人开心。现在可没那么回事了。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
We’re going to see an increasing divergence between what AI does in our personal lives and in daily productivity vs. what it can do in very deep domains like math, science, legal, coding and more.

Up to some threshold, capability was evenly felt across all domains because the models were just becoming mildly useful in general. Now, the deep domain work is about to go vertical. 

Most people won’t actually notice these benefits in their day to day life directly (indirectly they certainly will over time), but the experts in these fields will. And there’s no inherent ceiling to what capabilities are needed, unlike in the consumer space where needs can get met relatively straightforwardly.

This will often lead to a capability overhang, though, as many of these performance gains need to be applied to data sets and workflows in an applied way for that area of work. But this is ultimately how you get breakthroughs in life sciences, real world automation, new cyber capabilities, and more.
remarks.translation: 我们将看到，AI在个人生活和日常生产力中的应用，与其在数学、科学、法律、编程等深度领域的能力之间，差距会越来越大。在达到某个阈值之前，所有领域都能均匀感受到AI的能力提升，因为模型总体上只是变得稍微有用了一些。而现在，深度领域的工作即将迎来垂直突破。大多数人不会在日常生活中直接注意到这些好处（当然，随着时间的推移，他们会间接感受到），但这些领域的专家会。与消费者领域需求相对容易满足不同，深度领域所需的能力没有固有的上限。不过，这往往会导致能力过剩，因为许多性能提升需要以应用的方式融入特定工作领域的数据集和工作流程中。但最终，这正是生命科学、现实世界自动化、新型网络能力等领域取得突破的方式。
remarks.observation: 这条言论适合观察 AI 编程工具、设计到代码流程和软件生产方式的变化；需要结合产品发布或文档再做事实判断。

podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning (Redpoint)
podcasts.title: 第90集：AI先驱尤尔根·施密德胡伯谈当今AI现状
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today
podcasts.excerpt: 德高望重的科学家、AI 研究员于尔根·施密德胡伯博士被公认为该领域的先驱之一，他通过其实验室的工作，提出了当今 Transformer、LSTM 和递归自我改进背后的关键思想。他认为，真正的通用人工智能（AGI）仍受限于物理硬件，随着开源技术追赶封闭实验室的步伐，当今对 AI 数据中心的投资将迎来调整，而通往通用智能的道路在于人工好奇心与自主生成的实验，而非互联网数据。最后，他重新审视了主流的 AI 安全论点，并描绘了一幅自我复制的机器人社会最终殖民太阳系的宏大愿景。（0:00）引言（1:24）超人类 AI 还有多远？（2:27）ChatGPT 为何未让他感到意外（3:21）递归自我改进之路（9:01）AI 会起飞吗……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Dr. Jürgen Schmidhuber, a renowned scientist and AI researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers in the field, originated key ideas behind today's transformers, LSTMs, and recursive self-improvement through his lab's work. He argues that true AGI remains bottlenecked by physical hardware, that today's AI data center investments are headed for a correction as open-source keeps pace with closed labs, and that the path to general intelligence runs through artificial curiosity and self-generated experimentation rather than internet data. He closes by reconsidering mainstream AI safety arguments and offers a sweeping vision of self-replicating robot societies eventually colonizing the solar system. (0:00) Intro (1:24) How Close Is Superhuman AI? (2:27) Why ChatGPT Didn't Surprise Him (3:21) The Path to Recursive Self-Improvement (9:01) Will AI Takeoff…

podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning (Redpoint)
podcasts.title: 第91集：顶级AI分析师解析当今AI炒作周期
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 91: Top AI Analyst Unpacks Today's AI Hype Cycle
podcasts.excerpt: 科技界最受瞩目的分析师之一本尼迪克特·埃文斯做客雅各布·埃夫隆的节目。对话围绕本尼迪克特的核心论点展开：将人工智能的规模与过往平台变革（互联网、移动互联网、个人电脑）相类比，在分析层面毫无意义；更具建设性的做法是，研究那些技术在经济层面的实际演进过程，从而推断人工智能的价值将沉淀在何处。他认为，这次真正的不同在于，我们不知道人工智能的物理或科学边界，而过往变革中这些边界至少是可预知的——正是这种不确定性，既催生了通用人工智能的狂热，也助长了末日论调，却无法解决任何实质问题。本尼迪克特深入剖析了为何能力仍呈锯齿状分布，这意味着使用场景同样参差不齐；为何编程凭借可规模化验证的特性，成为首个真正的企业级应用场景；以及为何大多数消费级和企业级应用场景，仍有待创业者去发明……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Benedict Evans, one of tech's most widely-read analysts, joins Jacob Effron. The conversation centers on Benedict's core thesis that comparing AI's scale to past platform shifts (the internet, mobile, PCs) is analytically useless, and that the more productive move is studying how those previous technologies actually evolved economically to reason about where AI's value will accrue. He argues the one genuine difference this time is that we don't know AI's physical or scientific limits, unlike past shifts where the boundaries were at least knowable, and that this uncertainty is what fuels both AGI hype and doomerism without resolving anything. Benedict unpacks why capabilities remain jagged, meaning usage is jagged too, why coding became the first real enterprise use case thanks to scalable verification, and why most consumer and enterprise use cases still have to be invented by entrepreneurs rat…
